open_points.subject: owner-session cookie scope
open_points.text: carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin
open_points.question: Which cookie attributes and deployment constraint make “only to Registry's own origin” exact, given that cookies are scoped by host and path rather than by origin or port?
options: Use a host-only Secure HttpOnly SameSite cookie with Path=/ and require Registry to have an exclusive host name
Use a narrower interface path and permit the cookie to be sent to other ports on the same host
Treat the phrase as an application check rather than a browser-enforced cookie scope
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie with Path=/ and an exclusive Registry host name.

open_points.subject: import mapping of the project object
open_points.text: the mapping shows for the picks only: their rooms and pointers; the display name and alias each will arrive under
open_points.question: Where are the imported object's address, kind and characteristics shown and confirmed, even though the import carries the object and the owner must check the mapping before applying it?
options: Show every object value in the mapping and bind it to the confirmation
Import object values without showing them
Require the owner to replace some or all object values during mapping
open_points.default_guess: Show all object values unchanged and bind them to the confirmation.

open_points.subject: selection when project ids are duplicated in the import file
open_points.text: records only of projects the owner did not pick are neither checked, shown as conflicts nor imported, and take no part in the duplicate-id check
open_points.question: How can the owner pick one project when the file contains two project records with the same project id, and does picking that id bring both duplicate records into validation?
options: A duplicate project id makes the file unreadable before picks exist
Picking an id selects all records carrying it and then refuses them as duplicates
The mapping assigns occurrence identities so the owner can pick one duplicate
open_points.default_guess: Refuse duplicate project ids before presenting selectable projects.

open_points.subject: validation of unpicked malformed records
open_points.text: the mapping shows for the picks only: ... every malformed record and every id that conflicts with one production holds ... records only of projects the owner did not pick are neither checked
open_points.question: Are malformed records belonging only to unpicked projects reported or ignored?
options: Ignore every semantic defect confined to unpicked projects
Report all malformed records in the file but ignore their production conflicts
Refuse the whole file for any malformed record before project selection
open_points.default_guess: Ignore semantic defects confined to unpicked projects, except defects that prevent the file or project index from being read safely.

open_points.subject: failed replacement upload
open_points.text: until the import is accepted, another file is uploaded in that session, or the session ends; then it is dropped
open_points.question: Does an attempted upload that is oversized, unreadable or otherwise refused replace and drop the previously accepted uploaded file?
options: Only a successfully parsed upload replaces the previous file
Any received upload attempt immediately drops the previous file
A refused upload drops both files and leaves no upload pending
open_points.default_guess: Keep the previous file unless the new upload passes the initial file-level checks and produces a mapping.

open_points.subject: malformed imported object and pointer values
open_points.text: A brought-in record is malformed when: a required value is missing (A02); ... a pointer's type is not declared or its owner service is not the type's
open_points.question: Are an object kind outside its declared vocabulary, undeclared object characteristics, and a pointer with neither a nonblank uri nor a nonblank payload_ref malformed, and how are they reported?
options: Refuse each as a malformed brought-in record
Normalize or discard unsupported object values and pointer fields
Apply only the checks explicitly enumerated in A16
open_points.default_guess: Refuse all of them as malformed records.

open_points.subject: imported project time invariants
open_points.text: an `active` project has an archived instant or an `archived` one has none; ... a record was changed, archived or superseded before it was created, added or published
open_points.question: Must an archived imported project's last-changed instant equal its archived instant, as required by the Project revision/time rules, or may the two differ so long as neither precedes creation?
options: Require equality
Permit archived instant before last-changed instant
Permit either ordering after creation
open_points.default_guess: Require the archived and last-changed instants to be equal.

open_points.subject: file digest used for mapping and confirmation
open_points.text: The mapping names the file by its digest
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm and encoding identify the file, and is the digest computed over the exact uploaded bytes or a parsed/canonical representation?
options: A specified collision-resistant digest over the exact uploaded bytes
A specified digest over a canonicalized parsed file
A backend-selected digest and representation
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes with lowercase hexadecimal encoding.

open_points.subject: configuration parsing and malformed items
open_points.text: A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start
open_points.question: What is the configuration's concrete namespace and syntax, and what makes each non-secret item malformed rather than merely unusable, especially when configuration is supplied through an environment containing unrelated variables?
options: Define a closed Registry-prefixed configuration schema and reject unknown keys in that namespace
Treat the whole process environment as the configuration and reject every extra variable
Ignore unknown items and validate only recognized ones
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed Registry-specific namespace, ignore unrelated environment variables, and reject unknown Registry-prefixed items.

open_points.subject: backup-key rotation metadata
open_points.text: older backups stay encrypted with the key they were made with; the owner keeps that key in the vault until the last of them is deleted
open_points.question: How does the owner determine which retained key decrypts a particular backup after several key rotations?
options: Store a non-secret key identifier in authenticated backup metadata and record the same identifier in the vault
Derive the identifier from the key
Require the owner to try retained keys until one works
open_points.default_guess: Store an authenticated non-secret key identifier with each backup.

open_points.subject: audit sequence numbers after restore
open_points.text: numbering continues from the backup's last number, and the lost entries exist nowhere
open_points.question: If entries written after the backup had sequence numbers that are lost on restore, may those numbers be issued again, contrary to M09 and A15 saying sequence numbers are never reused and are ordered across every entry ever written?
options: Reuse numbers lost by the restore
Persist a high-water mark outside backups so numbers are never reused
Define restore as starting a new audit epoch with a separate identity
open_points.default_guess: Persist an audit high-water mark outside the restored store and continue above every number ever issued.

open_points.subject: migration closure after restoring a pre-import backup
open_points.text: Every change after the backup's instant is lost
open_points.question: If the first successful import occurred after the restored backup, how does Registry continue to refuse every later import when the migration closure has been lost, despite M10 saying it is present forever?
options: Keep the migration-closed fact outside the backed-up store and restore it separately
Permit the import again after such a restore
Require the owner to recreate the closure before enabling normal operation
open_points.default_guess: Keep and restore a durable migration-closed marker independently of the rollback point.

open_points.subject: create replay after restore
open_points.text: Every change after the backup's instant is lost
open_points.question: What happens when a caller retries a create or publish whose committed record and request id were lost by restore: must A01 still prevent a duplicate, or is replay safety explicitly limited to history retained in the restored store?
options: Preserve request-id outcomes outside the daily backup rollback point
Refuse or manually reconcile all potentially replayed pre-restore requests
Limit A01's guarantee to records present in the current restored store, allowing a new record
open_points.default_guess: State explicitly that A01 cannot survive rollback unless request-id outcomes are preserved separately; preserve them if the unconditional replay guarantee is retained.

open_points.subject: post-restore retention reconciliation
open_points.text: before configuring the tokens and starting it again ... Registry, which no longer holds those changes, cannot list them or tell when this is done
open_points.question: What prevents service mode from being enabled before the owner has reapplied every erased, restricted or ended state, and what exact external record is authoritative enough to determine that reconciliation is complete?
options: Require a durable external reconciliation manifest and an explicit completion marker Registry verifies
Rely solely on the owner's manual procedure with no technical gate
Keep erasure and restriction tombstones outside rollback-capable backups
open_points.default_guess: Use an external reconciliation manifest plus a verified completion marker before service tokens are accepted.

open_points.subject: removed artifact types in persisted pointers
open_points.text: A release that removes a type keeps every pointer of it ... After the removal, publishing that type and 'read the latest artifact of a type' for it are refused as an unknown type
open_points.question: How can a retained pointer still satisfy M05's rule that its type is one of the vocabulary the specification declares, and how do output schemas represent a removed type that is now “unknown”?
options: Keep removed types as declared historical/tombstoned vocabulary entries that are readable but not writable
Allow stored pointers to carry arbitrary legacy type strings outside the current vocabulary
Forbid type removal while any pointer of the type exists
open_points.default_guess: Retain removed types as tombstoned historical vocabulary entries accepted in reads but refused for publish, latest lookup and withdrawal.

open_points.subject: service-token abuse controls
open_points.text: authentication_credential_abuse: guessing, credential stuffing, session and token lifecycle at every human and machine boundary; scope, revocation, replay, who owns the abuse controls
open_points.question: What abuse control, if any, applies to repeated wrong service-token attempts, and who owns detecting or throttling them? A13 defines only owner sign-in lockout, while A09 and A17 define rights and startup validation.
options: Registry rate-limits failed service authentication
Infrastructure detects and limits it, with Registry doing no throttling
No throttling is provided because the service API is network-restricted, stated explicitly as the accepted risk
open_points.default_guess: Assign detection and rate limiting to the infrastructure and state explicitly that Registry performs no service-token throttling.
